problemStatement.formal: Let f3(n) be the maximal size of a subset of {0,1,2}^n containing no three collinear points. Is f3(n) = o(3^n)?
problemStatement.plain: Is the maximum cap set in {0,1,2}^n subexponential relative to 3^n?
whyMatters: Connected to coding theory and finite geometry
Led to polynomial method breakthrough by Ellenberg-Gijswijt

open: Exact value of lim sup f3(n)^{1/n}
knownResults.goal: YES - proved via density Hales-Jewett theorem

currentState.focus: Added product-derived lower bounds and general power bound

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Main theorem f3(n) = o(3^n) proved from DHJ axiom. Exact values for n=0..4. Product structure, binary cube lower bound, and derived bounds for n=5..8.
builtItems: IsCapSet, f3(n) definitions and basic properties
Exact values: f3_0, f3_1, f3_2, f3_3, f3_4
insights: DHJ axiom is the minimal assumption needed for the main theorem
Meshulam axiom only needed for f3(3)=9 and f3(4)=20 upper bounds
Product structure gives strong lower bounds without explicit constructions
f3_power_lower_bound: f3(kn) >= f3(n)^k generalizes all product bounds
